{"id": "6579f45f-5fad-4a7d-8b81-cbc11f651af3", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_zc068GmGrvBMWcEbaqeBf2", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Security Hub CSPM controls for Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"## [Bedrock.1] Amazon Bedrock data sources should be encrypted with customer managed AWS KMS keys\\\\n\\\\n**Related requirements:** NIST.800-53.r5 AU-9,\\\\nNIST.800-53.r5 CA-9(1), NIST.800-53.r5 CM-3(6), NIST.800-53.r5 SC-7(10),\\\\nNIST.800-53.r5 SC-12(2), NIST.800-53.r5 SC-13, NIST.800-53.r5 SC-28, NIST.800-53.r5\\\\nSC-28(1), NIST.800-53.r5 SI-7(6)\\\\n\\\\n**Category:** Protect > Data protection >\\\\nEncryption of data at rest\\\\n\\\\n**Severity:** Medium\\\\n\\\\n**Resource type:**\\\\n`AWS::Bedrock::DataSource`\\\\n\\\\n**AWS Config rule:**\\\\nbedrock-data-source-encryption-enabled\\\\n\\\\n**Schedule type:** Change triggered\\\\n\\\\n**Parameters:** None\\\\n\\\\nThis control checks whether an Amazon Bedrock data source is encrypted at rest with a\\\\ncustomer managed AWS KMS key. The control fails if the data source isn\\'t encrypted with a\\\\ncustomer managed KMS key. The control doesn\\'t evaluate data sources that belong to a\\\\nmanaged knowledge base.\\\\n\\\\nBy default, Amazon Bedrock encrypts data source content with AWS managed keys. Using\\\\na customer managed KMS key gives you full control over the encryption key lifecycle,\\\\nincluding rotation, access policies, and auditing through AWS CloudTrail. This helps meet\\\\ncompliance requirements that mandate customer-controlled encryption for sensitive data\\\\ningested into knowledge bases.\\\\n\\\\n### Remediation\\\\n\\\\nTo encrypt your Amazon Bedrock data source with a customer managed KMS key, see\\\\nModify a data source for your\\\\nAmazon Bedrock knowledge base in the *Amazon\\\\nBedrock User Guide*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/bedrock-controls.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"AWS SDK for C++: Aws::Bedrock::Model::CreateModelCustomizationJobRequest Class Reference\",\"context\":\"## \u25c6CustomModelKmsKeyIdHasBeenSet()\\\\n\\\\n| | | | | | | |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bool Aws::Bedrock::Model::CreateModelCustomizationJobRequest::CustomModelKmsKeyIdHasBeenSet | ( | | ) | const | | inline |\\\\n\\\\nThe custom model is encrypted at rest using this key.\\\\n\\\\nDefinition at line 160 of file CreateModelCustomizationJobRequest.h\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-cpp/latest/api/aws-cpp-sdk-bedrock/html/class_aws_1_1_bedrock_1_1_model_1_1_create_model_customization_job_request.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Considerations for addressing the core dimensions of responsible AI for Amazon Bedrock applications | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"### Built-in security and privacy of Amazon Bedrock\\\\n\\\\nWith Amazon Bedrock, if we look from a data privacy and localization perspective, AWS does not store your data\u2014if we don\u2019t store it, it can\u2019t leak, it can\u2019t be seen by model vendors, and it can\u2019t be used by AWS for any other purpose. The only data we store is operational metrics\u2014for example, for accurate billing, AWS collects metrics on how many tokens you send to a specific Amazon Bedrock model and how many tokens you receive in a model output. And, of course, if you create a fine-tuned model, we need to store that in order for AWS to host it for you. Data used in your API requests remains in the AWS Region of your choosing\u2014API requests to the Amazon Bedrock API to a specific Region will remain completely within that Region.\\\\n\\\\nIf we look at data security, a common adage is that if it moves, encrypt it. Communications to, from, and within Amazon Bedrock are encrypted in transit\u2014Amazon Bedrock doesn\u2019t have a non-TLS endpoint. Another adage is that if it doesn\u2019t move, encrypt it. Your fine-tuning data and model will by default be encrypted using AWS managed AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys, but you have the option to use your own KMS keys.\\\\n\\\\nWhen it comes to identity and access management, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls who is authorized to use Amazon Bedrock resources. For each model, you can explicitly allow or deny access to actions. For example, one team or account could be allowed to provision capacity for Amazon Titan Text, but not Anthropic models. You can be as broad or as granular as you need to be.\\\\n\\\\nLooking at network data flows for Amazon Bedrock API access, it\u2019s important to remember that traffic is encrypted at all time. If you\u2019re using Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), you can use AWS PrivateLink to provide your VPC with private connectivity through the regional network direct to the frontend fleet of Amazon Bedrock, mitigating exposure of your VPC to internet traffic with an internet gateway. Similarly, from a corporate data center perspective, you can set up a VPN or AWS Direct Connect connection to privately connect to a VPC, and from there you can have that traffic sent to Amazon Bedrock over PrivateLink. This should negate the need for your on-premises systems to send Amazon Bedrock related traffic over the\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/considerations-for-addressing-the-core-dimensions-of-responsible-ai-for-amazon-bedrock-applications/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Model customization access and security\",\"context\":\"### (Optional) Encrypt model customization jobs and artifacts\\\\n\\\\nEncrypt the input and output data, customization jobs, or inference requests made to\\\\ncustom models. For more information, see Encryption of custom models\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-job-access-security.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Security best practices to consider while fine-tuning models in Amazon Bedrock | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Security in Amazon Bedrock\\\\n\\\\nCloud security at AWS is the highest priority. Amazon Bedrock prioritizes security through a comprehensive approach to protect customer data and AI workloads.\\\\n\\\\nAmazon Bedrock is built with security at its core, offering several features to protect your data and models. The main aspects of its security framework include:\\\\n\\\\n* **Access control** \u2013 This includes features such as:\\\\n + Fine-grained access control using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)\\\\n + Resource-based policies to control access to specific Amazon Bedrock resources\\\\n* **Data encryption** \u2013 Amazon Bedrock offers the following encryption:\\\\n + Data at rest is encrypted using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)\\\\n + Data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher\\\\n* **Network security** \u2013 Amazon Bedrock offers several security options, including:\\\\n + Support for AWS PrivateLink to establish private connectivity between your virtual private cloud (VPC) and Amazon Bedrock\\\\n + VPC endpoints for secure communication within your AWS environment\\\\n* **Compliance** \u2013 Amazon Bedrock is in alignment with various industry standards and regulations, including HIPAA, SOC, and PCI DSS\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/security-best-practices-to-consider-while-fine-tuning-models-in-amazon-bedrock/\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"AWS Security Hub CSPM launches AI Security Best Practices standard with 31 automated controls - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS Security Hub CSPM has introduced the AI Security Best Practices standard, which includes 31 automated security controls for detecting misalignments between security best practices and deployed AI resources. These controls cover critical security domains such as network isolation, encryption, VPC placement, KMS key usage, private container registry requirements, and authorization controls. The standard applies to various components of AI infrastructure, including Bedrock AgentCore runtimes, gateways, memory stores, custom browsers, SageMaker notebook instances, endpoints, models, monitoring jobs, and feature groups.
